steps.title: Feedforward plus feedback
steps.say: PID here is the feedforward guess **plus** a correction that grows with the error.

marks.label: feedforward: the power to hold the speed

steps.title: Open ShooterConstants.java
steps.say: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `ShooterConstants` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

steps.title: Find kV
steps.say: Search for `FLYWHEEL_KV`. Set `FLYWHEEL_CONTROL = FEEDFORWARD` and try kV 0.05, 0.10, 0.12, restarting each time.

steps.title: Start the robot
steps.say: Your code only runs once it's built and started.

waitFor.hint: press Start and wait for Running.

steps.title: Enable in Teleop
steps.say: Pick **Teleop** and press **Enable**. Robot code runs only while it's enabled.

steps.title: Watch the speed
steps.say: Hold **U**, then tap **K** (A) to launch a game piece. Feedforward never notices the dip. In AdvantageScope, search for `FlywheelVelocity`, then drag **Subsystem/Shooter/FlywheelVelocity** onto the **Left Axis**.

steps.title: Add kP
steps.say: Switch to `PID`, keep your kV, and raise `FLYWHEEL_KP`: 0.05, 0.2, 1.0. Now the dip recovers. Too big and a real robot buzzes.

waitFor.hint: raise kP and watch the recovery.

steps.title: Measure it
steps.say: Aim for a recovery under about 0.8 seconds. In AdvantageScope, search for `RecoverySeconds`, then drag **Subsystem/Shooter/RecoverySeconds** onto the **Right Axis**.

steps.title: Check your work
steps.say: When it runs the way you expect, open the lesson chip and press **Verify**. Each checkpoint tells you what it's looking for if it doesn't pass yet.
